_doc: Inflation benchmarks for retrospective editions dated in 2010: the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at each cutoff. End-2009 state of the verified 2009 register, plus the 2010 current-year targets set earlier (Czechia 2% from January 2010, Türkiye 6.5%, Colombia 3%, Korea's 2010–12 target) and changes announced during 2010; each new source URL was fetched and its claim checked, and sources are shown only once published.
note: Three economies had no headline-CPI target: the Federal Reserve had no numerical target (2.0% is an analytical benchmark), the RBI's objectives referred to the wholesale price index (the benchmark is the RBI's stated end-of-fiscal-year WPI projection), and the Bank of Thailand targeted core inflation. Benchmarks apply to the headline CPI series used here. Each benchmark is the target for the current calendar year as publicly known at the cutoff; China's is the government's annual CPI objective, announced each March (until then the previous year's applies); Czechia's 2% target applies from January 2010 (announced in March 2007). Where a range was set, its midpoint is used; for the euro area's ‘below but close to 2%’, 1.9%. Sources are listed only if published on or before the edition’s last eligible day.

US.wording: No numerical inflation target. FOMC projections released 24 Nov 2009: central tendency for longer-run PCE inflation 1.7–2.0% (unchanged), reflecting participants' assessments of the rate that best satisfies the dual mandate. 2.0% headline CPI is this monitor's analytical benchmark.
US.index: PCE price index (FOMC projections); benchmark applied to headline CPI
